plaques.text:
THE FIRST RINGER — SERA, THE LAMPWRIGHT

She rang the First Bell with burned hands, having carried the vigil flame through a night the wind hated.

Her fate: she never again stood in a light she had not made. She was deemed worthy because she STOOD STILL while it hurt.

Stand in her light. Do not leave it.

THE SECOND RINGER — HARLAN, THE TOLLWRIGHT

He rang the Second Bell only after every debt in the quarter was paid — most of them out of his own purse.

His fate: he died owning nothing but the rope. He was deemed worthy because the ledger balanced.

Kindle all three votives. Light is paid forward here.

THE THIRD RINGER — BRIDE VESPERINE, THE CHORISTER

She rang the Third Bell as the last note of a psalm sung alone in an empty quire.

Her fate: no choir would have her after — her voice made theirs sound like counting. She was deemed worthy for singing the day in its ORDER.

Ring her day: dawn, then noon, then dusk.

THE FOURTH RINGER — SER ODILE, WARDEN-AT-ARMS

She rang the Fourth Bell with her shield arm, the right one being occupied with dying.

Her fate: the wound kept her from every war after; she drilled children in the yard instead. Deemed worthy because she rang WHILE losing.

Her echoes still drill. Put them down.

THE FIFTH RINGER — BROTHER CASSIAN, THE WATCHER

He rang the Fifth Bell at the exact instant dawn crossed the sill, having watched forty nights for it without once facing away.

His fate: his eyes never recovered the dark. Deemed worthy because he LOOKED where the light would come from.

Turn every watcher to the east.

THE SIXTH RINGER — VEY, WHO WAS PAID

A sellsword rang the Sixth Bell for coin, because no believer was left standing that year.

His fate: he refused the purse at the rope's end and no one ever learned why. Deemed worthy the moment the coin stopped mattering.

His hired blade stands the room. Best it, without hiring one of your own.

THE SEVENTH RINGER — MOTHER LOAM, THE GRAVEDIGGER

She rang the Seventh Bell once for every soul she had put down that winter — six hundred pulls, one grief at a time.

Her fate: her hands forgot how to open. Deemed worthy because she counted every one and skipped none.

The unquiet she buried rise here. Return them, one at a time.

THE EIGHTH RINGER — MASTER HALIARD, THE ASTRONOMER

He rang the Eighth Bell by arithmetic, at an hour he had computed nine years in advance, alone against every almanac.

His fate: he was right, and never forgiven for it. Deemed worthy because the heavens kept his appointment.

Ring his sky in its order: east, zenith, west, nadir, north.

THE NINTH RINGER — WREN, THE MIDWIFE

She rang the Ninth Bell one-handed. The other arm held a child born in the same minute, because neither task would wait.

Her fate: every child she caught after was said to sleep through any bell. Deemed worthy for holding BOTH.

Hold her hour. It is longer than it looks.

THE TENTH RINGER — GORE THE GATEWRIGHT

He rang the Tenth Bell with the same pull that shut the flood-gates, one rope in each fist, because the river and the hour came at once.

His fate: the town kept dry and never knew. Deemed worthy for facing every gate HOME before himself.

Turn all four to face the road home — south, where you came from.

THE ELEVENTH RINGER — THE FERRYWRIGHT ANSA

She rang the Eleventh Bell from mid-river, standing on the keel of her own capsized ferry, so the crossing bell would not miss its hour.

Her fate: she never reached either bank; the river kept her fare. Deemed worthy because the hour arrived DRY.

Her drowned crew still makes the crossing. See them over.

THE TWELFTH RINGER — UNNAMED, THE LAST HAND

The Twelfth gave up their name at the rope, so the bell would carry NOTHING of them but the ring.

Their fate: no grave, no ballad, no face in the glass. Deemed worthy because nothing was kept back.

What is left of them keeps this room. Give them rest, Thirteenth.

THE LAST DOOR

Twelve rang before you. Twelve rooms remember how, and what it cost.

Keep all twelve trials, and the bell itself will draw the bolt.

watcher_puzzles.done_toast: The watchers face the morrow. The Fifth is satisfied.
Four gates face the road home. The Tenth is satisfied.
